newsitem.title: SWEDEN: New Swedish prime minister aid to vet budget cuts.
newsitem.headline: New Swedish prime minister aid to vet budget cuts.

text.p: Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson said on Tuesday he was moving former Defence Minister Thage Peterson into a position where he could review some of the budget cuts in Sweden.

Annoucing some limited changes to cabinet, Persson said Peterson, as a member of his inner cabinet, or a close group of advisors, would focus on revising budget cutbacks that have not had the desired effect.
Peterson, a veteran with the ruling Social Democrat party, said self-criticism was necessary.
"We agreed on many painful cutbacks that have been rough on many people," Peterson said. "An important goal is to win the general elections in (September) 1998."
Since Persson took leadership of the ruling Social Democrats in March 1996, succeeding retiring Ingvar Carlsson, he has implemented widespread cuts.
A recent opinion poll showed support for the Social Democrats had fallen below 30 percent for the first time since 1991, with Swedes critical of the cuts and high unemployment.
Persson said Peterson made it clear last year that he would only remain defence minister for a limited time.
"But I do not want him to quit the inner cabinet as he has so much experience and knowledge," Persson said.
Other cabinet changes announced on Tuesday included appointing former Industry and Commerce Minister Bjorn von Sydow to the defence portfolio.
Junior Cabinet Minister in the Prime Minister's office, Leif Pagrotsky, will replace von Sydow.
